claim: The note calls まちます the plain/dictionary form, but the deck already taught me (chapter-0 note) that the base verb is まつ, and every verb I know ends in ます.
evidence: Back note: 'Plain/dictionary form of まってください (please wait) — て-form (まって) + ください makes the polite request.' Compare chapter-0/chotto-matte-kudasai note: 'まって is the て-form of まつ (matsu, "to wait") plus ください'.
fix: Reword the note to say まちます is the ます form of the verb behind まってください (whose dictionary form is まつ), not its dictionary form.

claim: The note sends me to the まちます card 'for the plain dictionary form', repeating the false label and contradicting the chapter-0 note that names まつ as the base.
evidence: Back note: 'て-form of まちます (wait) + ください — see that card for the plain dictionary form.' Chapter-0 note: 'まって is the て-form of まつ (matsu, "to wait")'.
fix: Say 'see that card for the ます form', or name まつ as the dictionary form.

claim: The note points to a card titled 'What a very old clock!' that I never meet, and to ほんとうに 'below', which means nothing in a shuffled deck.
evidence: Back note: 'See the card "What a very old clock!" for とても used with an adjective. Similar to ほんとうに ("really", below)'. The real card (totemo-furui-tokei-ne) reads 'It's a very old clock, isn't it?'.
fix: Quote the real card's English and drop 'below'.

claim: The note points to a card titled 'Yeah, it's really cold.', but the card I meet reads differently, so I cannot find it by its English.
evidence: Back note: 'See "Yeah, it's really cold." for ほんとうに used with an adjective.' The real card (hontouni-samui-ne) reads 'Yeah, it really is cold, isn't it?'.
fix: Quote the real card's English exactly.

claim: ふじさん ends in さん, which the deck taught me only as the honorific 'Mr., Mrs., Ms.' (and the number 3), so I read it as 'Mr. Fuji' with nothing on the back to explain.
evidence: Back: 'Answer: Mt. Fuji / Says: fujisan', no note. Earlier: chapter-1 さん | 'Mr., Mrs., Ms., Miss'; chapter-2 さん | '3'.
fix: Add a one-line note that this さん means 'mountain' and is not the honorific.

claim: The Production front 'Place' fits ばしょ ('Location', Lesson 9) just as well, and only the back's note separates them.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Other / Place'. Earlier card chapter-9/basho-location: ばしょ | 'Location'. The difference lives only in the note: 'ところ describes what kind of place somewhere is'.
fix: Add a hint such as 'what kind of place somewhere is, as in どんな___' to the front.

claim: This card and the base card kirei both ask for 'pretty' and both mention 'clean', but one wants きれいな and the other きれい, with nothing on either front to choose between them.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Other / Pretty / also "clean, tidy"' (answer きれいな). Base chapter-10/kirei Production FRONT: 'Other / Pretty, beautiful, clean' (answer きれい).
fix: Cut one of the two, or give this one a hint like 'the form that goes before a noun'.

claim: 'Who is it?' is already the English of だれですか, so I will answer はい、だれですか; nothing on the front asks for the polite どなた.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Greetings / Yes. Who is it?' (answer はい、どなたですか). Earlier: chapter-2-extras/p102-dare-desu-ka だれですか | 'Who is it?'.
fix: Add a hint such as 'polite, answering the door' to the front.

claim: The hint names the word and the form I am being asked to produce, so the front no longer tests whether I can make やすくないです.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'This wine is not cheap. / Use やすい (yasui, "inexpensive") in the negative, not たかい (takai, "expensive")'.
fix: Shorten the hint to something like 'not the word for expensive', or drop it: 'not cheap' already points at やすい.

claim: The note says いい is 'the one irregular い-adjective', yet this same unit teaches かっこいい, which also ends in いい, and nothing tells me whether it negates like いい or regularly.
evidence: Back note: 'いい (ii) is the one irregular い-adjective: its negative is よくないです (yokunai desu), never いくない'. Same unit: cool | かっこいい | 'Cool / stylish, good-looking', no note on its negative.
fix: Say adjectives ending in いい (like かっこいい) follow the same よくない change, or drop 'the one'.

claim: The romaji on this card spells ええ and ほんとうに differently from the base cards built on the same words, so the two read like different words.
evidence: This card: 'Says: ee, hontō ni ii tenki desu ne'. Base chapter-10/hontouni-samui-ne: 'Says: ē, hontōni samui desu ne'; chapter-10/hontouni: 'Says: hontōni'.
fix: Romanize ええ and ほんとうに the same way on every card in the chapter.
